quotes.text: This isn't a technicality, it's structural. Contracts are obligations. Technical controls are the enforcement mechanisms.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Frames the core argument that legal agreements come before any technical Copilot configuration.

quotes.text: A Copilot license isn't a skeleton key. It's more like a building permit with a bouncer attached. The permit defines what can legally exist, and the bouncer enforces who's allowed past the rope.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable analogy separating licensing from access control.

quotes.text: Here's the clarification you need to tattoo onto your brain. Licenses enable Copilot features, but Copilot only surfaces data a user already has permission to see via Microsoft Graph.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the key fact behind Copilot oversharing risk in one sentence.

quotes.text: Governance that isn't system driven isn't governance at all. It's a bedtime story. If you want rules that actually function, they must be hard coded directly into the tools your employees already use.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear thesis that governance must be enforced technically, not by memos.

chapters.title: What really flips when you turn on Copilot
Contracts: Product Terms and the DPA
Licenses and RBAC: the locks on every door
Data exposure: Copilot mirrors your permissions
Technical controls: Admin Center, Purview and Defender
Wrap-up: three checks for your tenant

takeaways: Copilot is governed by the Microsoft Product Terms and the Data Protection Addendum before any toggle is flipped, so legal review and residency mapping come first.
A Copilot license grants features, not permissions: Copilot only surfaces what a user can already access through Microsoft Graph, so RBAC and permission hygiene define the real exposure.
Effective Copilot governance is system-enforced: Purview labels, DLP, DSPM for AI and Defender endpoint DLP turn policies into rules users cannot bypass.
hook: Think enabling Microsoft 365 Copilot is just a switch in the admin center? This episode is for IT admins, security and compliance leads who need to understand what contracts, licenses, RBAC and data controls actually govern before rollout. You will learn which Purview, Defender and licensing steps to take so Copilot becomes a disciplined enabler instead of an oversharing risk.
